component.name: Trace Commons
component.summary: Review and contribute your coding sessions

description.p: Trace Commons contributes the sessions you have with coding agents to an open corpus, with your explicit consent for each one. Nothing leaves your machine until you have seen exactly what it contains.
The application watches the session folders you nominate, and nothing else. It will not guess: until you say which folders to watch, it watches none of them.
Every session is scanned for secrets and personal information and shown to you in full before anything is sent. You decide per session, or arm a project you trust to contribute without asking.

When you mark a session as failed or partly successful, you can now add a short written note saying what went wrong. Writing one is optional and skipping it changes nothing. Nothing else in a trace can carry that: the transcript records what the agent did, not what you expected it to do instead.

The note is stored exactly as you write it. This is the one exception to the redaction that covers everything else -- file paths and email addresses elsewhere in a session are replaced with placeholders before upload, and replacing them in a note would remove the explanation it exists to give. Treat it as writing about your own work, and leave out anything you would not want in the corpus.
One protection still applies. If a note appears to contain a credential, the upload is refused and you are asked to remove it rather than having it quietly masked, so you know to change the key.

When you approve a session, the app now asks whether it did what you asked: worked, partly, or failed. Nothing in a transcript answers that question. An agent that stops has not thereby succeeded, and a run that recorded no error has not thereby done the job, so you are asked rather than guessed at.

Answering is optional and never blocks approving. Skipping is a normal answer -- the session is recorded as unknown, which is what every session before this release recorded. The question appears on the preview sheet, and each project group offers the same three answers for sending everything it has waiting at once.

The answer records whether the task was finished, and nothing else. It is not a rating: a run can finish the job by a route you disliked, or fail while doing the right thing, and those are a different question this does not ask. Your answer is not part of the preview shown above it, and the preview says so.

Nothing in the Linux app has changed in this release. It fixes the macOS app, where finishing setup could leave you looking at the last screen of it forever: the button that ends setup recorded that you were finished but did not move you on, so the app sat there as though the button had not been pressed. Every platform is published at one version number, so this one exists on Linux with nothing behind it.

You can now turn down a whole project from the waiting list itself. Each project already offered a way to send everything it had waiting; there was no way to say the opposite without going to Settings and finding the project in a list. The waiting list now offers both, and asks you to confirm, telling you how many traces it is about to clear.

Turning a project down also does what it says. Until now it stopped future sessions being offered but left everything already waiting sitting in the list, so the traces you had just declined stayed on screen. They are now cleared, and anything you had already approved is still sent -- a decision you have already made is not taken back by a preference you set afterwards.
The choice remains reversible. Setting the project back to being offered brings its waiting sessions back, including finished ones whose files will never change again.

Declining a trace now sticks. Choosing "Not this one" used to set aside only the exact conversation as it stood at that moment, so the moment you typed another message the same conversation came back to the waiting list, and it kept coming back for as long as you kept working in it. A declined conversation is now left alone for good, and in projects set to send automatically it is no longer picked up on your behalf after you have said no.

Cards are honest about what they cover. A very large conversation has its biggest delegated transcripts left out to keep it within its size limit, and the card now says so instead of describing a trimmed conversation as though it were whole. The conversation itself is never trimmed.

Traces that cannot be sent no longer wait forever. One too large to send is now recorded as refused when you approve it, rather than staying in the list offering a choice that could never succeed. A session the app cannot read at all is reported instead of quietly disappearing.

The app now costs almost nothing when it has nothing to do. It was re-reading and re-hashing every waiting session on every check, including the ones it had no room to offer you, which kept a processor core busy continuously and read gigabytes a minute to no purpose. It also no longer rewrites its records when nothing has changed.

Privacy risk is also labelled more honestly. A trace where the scrubber found a secret and removed it was being marked high risk, which described the scrubber working rather than anything left behind, and held those traces back from being accepted. High is now reserved for content redaction did not resolve. A privacy filter that could not examine the text is treated as high risk rather than as clean.

The watcher no longer re-reads and re-hashes every waiting session on every poll, so the app stops working when there is nothing to do. The daily upload budget can be changed without editing a file, and the app says when uploads are waiting on it.
The history screen now updates when a submission lands, instead of showing the counts it had at launch.

The queue no longer builds a preview for every waiting session at once, so opening the app does not pin the machine. Large sessions render without freezing, and queue rows are created as they scroll into view.
Submit a trace from the queue row, or every trace in a project, without opening the preview first. Opening a very large session no longer freezes the window.
Submit a trace straight from the queue, or every trace in a project, without opening the preview first. Session scanning now streams files instead of reading them whole.
